newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish yields seen rising on budget trouble news.
newsitem.headline: Polish yields seen rising on budget trouble news.

text.p: Polish treasury yields are expected to rise at upcoming primary auctions on news that the finance ministry was having trouble financing the budget.

Poland's treasury had temporarily lost liquidity last week and was unable to pay some public sector workers, which dealers said meant that banks would test higher yields knowing that the finance ministry was badly in need of funds.

"Yields are bound to rise as banks test lower prices, the benchmark 52-week paper yield could break 21.55 percent," said Wojciech Kowalczyk, senior dealer at Bank Handlowy SA. The 52-week T-bill yielded 21.45 percent at last week's auction.
Dealers said that with little foreign or corporate bids expected at Monday's 1.4 billion zloty primary T-bill tender, banks would most probably test new maximum yields.
"It seems the 900 million zloty offer of 52-week bills will not be met unless investors try to lock in at higher yields," said Krzysztof Kozuchowski, dealer at ING bank.
Secondary trade was very light on Thursday with quotes straddling average yield levels from yesterday's auction.
The zloty closed a touch lower against the basket after listless trade after a light morning currency buying trend sparked by position rebuilding, dealers said.
"Trade was basically sideways today with dollar/mark changes creating the only movement on an otherwise calm market," said Mateusz Bieniek of Societe Generale in Warsaw.
On Wedneday Polish banks cut currency exposure to lengthen zloty positions to take advantage of high-yielding local currency deposits for the weekend, dealers said.
The zloty closed at 1.47/1.44 percent from the trading band centre, weaker than Wednesday's 1.52/1.49 percent close.
It closed at 3.2340/48 to the dollar, down from 3.2230/40 on Wednesday and at 1.8752/57 to the mark, up from 1.8779/84.

On the money market overnight rates fell to 22.00/22.20 percent from 22.20/22.40 percent at opening despite a one billion zloty NBP-bill sale, while tomorrow/next rates slipped to 22.20/22.30 from 22.25/22.40 despite a 630 million drainage.
Dealers said the market remained overliquid and banks tried to place cash ahead of the week-end amid today's outflows.
